text: Whoa, why does my leg feel like pins and needles?
Sit on it too long, and the nerve inside your leg gets squeezed - signals can't get through cleanly.
The second the pressure's off, the nerve starts firing again - just unevenly, all at once, and that's the tingle.
This happens a lot when you sit cross-legged for too long - that's exactly the position that presses on the nerve behind your knee.

There's an old Korean folk trick - wet your finger, draw a cross on your forehead, and the numbness is supposed to go away. Turns out the nerve was just about to reset on its own - the cross gets the credit.
Give it about a minute, and the nerve settles back down - the tingling fades on its own.
